subject: using package lmmfit to generate R-squared for a programmatically generated list of mixed effects models

messages.author: 2b27719db7267c87
messages.subject: using package lmmfit to generate R-squared for a programmatically generated list of mixed effects models
parts:
Hi D-RUG folks.

Does anyone know how to generate R-squared statistics for a programmatically generated list of lme models? Here is what I tried:

require(nlme)

mod.func <- function(var.name) {
  lme(as.formula(paste("outcome.var", "~", var.name)), 
      ~ 1| group, data = dat, method = "ML")
}

vars <- names(dat[ , setdiff(names(dat), c("group", "outcome.var"))])
mods <- lapply(vars, mod.func)

require(lmmfit)
sapply(mods, lmmR2)

Error in paste("outcom.var", "~", var.name) : 
  object 'var.name' not found

Bonnie

​

messages.subject: Re: [D-RUG]: using package lmmfit to generate R-squared for a programmatically generated list of mixed effects models
parts:
Sorry, Vince. Here is a reproducible example using the Orthodont data set.

require(nlme)
require(lmmfit)

# How lmmR2() normally works:
mod1 <- lme(distance ~ age, ~ 1 | Subject, data = Orthodont)
lmmR2(mod1)

# Attempting to use lmmR2 on a programmatically generated list of models:
mod.func <- function(var.name) {
  lme(as.formula(paste("distance", "~", var.name)), 
      ~ 1| Subject, data = Orthodont)
}
vars <- c("age", "Sex")
mods <- lapply(vars, mod.func)
sapply(mods, lmmR2)
​

Bonnie

messages.author: b35e99045f6c74c2
messages.subject: Re: [D-RUG]: using package lmmfit to generate R-squared for a programmatically generated list of mixed effects models
parts:
Hi Bonnie,

Using do.call() will do the trick:

mod.func <- function(var.name) {
  form <- as.formula(paste("distance", "~", var.name)) 
  do.call(lme, list(fixed=form, random=~ 1|Subject, data = Orthodont))
}

> mods <- lapply(vars, mod.func)
> sapply(mods, lmmR2)
[1] 0.2564651 0.1530632

The backstory is that lme uses non-standard evaluation to get the fixed part of the model, which fails when this is a function call (as in paste(...)). do.call evaluates beforehand, solving the problem.

HTH,
Vince
